tail.summary: The authors propose EdgeLM, an in-context demonstration retrieval framework for table-centric LLM prediction that selects edge evidence rather than similarity-matched examples: data edges (nearby examples with different ground-truth labels) and model edges (similar examples the deployed model previously misclassified), requiring no retraining. Tested across five data wrangling tasks, fifteen datasets, and five open-weight and proprietary LLMs, EdgeLM consistently achieves the best or near-best performance in every setting, with ablations showing the two edge-evidence types provide complementary benefits.

tail.title: Pun Intended: Multi-Agent Translation of Wordplay with Contrastive Learning and Phonetic-Semantic Embeddings
tail.summary: They compare three LLM-based approaches to translating puns from English to French: a discriminator-guided baseline, a phonetic-semantic embedding-guided reasoning pipeline, and an iterative multi-agent evaluation system, entered in the CLEF JOKER 2025 Task 2 pun-translation competition. The multi-agent and guided chain-of-thought systems placed first and second under expert human evaluation, even though their BLEU and BERTScore gains over the baseline were only modest.

tail.title: Searching for Sound-Meaning Collisions: Graph-Based Affordance Retrieval and Multi-Evaluator Ranking for Pun Translation at CLEF 2026 JOKER Task 2
tail.summary: They frame pun translation as discovery: a retrieval system searches target-language semantic and phonological neighborhoods for sound-meaning affordances, LLMs generate competing translations exploiting them, and a multi-perspective generate-and-rank system picks among candidates, evaluated for CLEF 2026 JOKER Task 2. Generators actively exploit retrieved affordances, evaluators concentrate on stronger sound-meaning bridges, and exact phonological collisions are selected disproportionately often when available, though many puns yield no usable affordances, marking retrieval the central bottleneck.

tail.title: Investigating Artificial Intelligence Digital Sovereignty in Mobile Shopping Apps: A Case Study of Nigeria
tail.summary: They combine forensic analysis of selected Android e-commerce apps with contextual document analysis to assess AI transparency and digital sovereignty in Nigerian mobile shopping apps, using an interpretive methodology. AI features are widely implemented across the apps, but disclosure about their use remains limited, and a socio-economic analysis finds growing dependence on these platforms alongside only moderate AI awareness and uneven interaction patterns among users, with no quantitative transparency scores reported.

tail.title: MicroEvo: Knowledge-Guided LLM Sampling for Efficient Microarchitecture Design Space Exploration
tail.summary: MicroEvo couples off-the-shelf LLMs with Monte Carlo Tree Search for multi-objective microarchitecture design space exploration, adding a Pareto-aware tree policy, active knowledge accumulation, and state-aware search directives, tested against NSGA-II including on a complex industrial-scale core. It improves Pareto-front quality by up to 36.2% over NSGA-II and achieves 10.6x higher search efficiency, demonstrating strong scalability to the industrial-scale design case.

tail.title: CourseGraph: Finding overlaps and differences in Computer Science courses across universities
tail.summary: CourseGraph extracts course titles, descriptions, and learning outcomes from university webpages, embeds them with a BERT-based model, computes pairwise course similarity, and feeds this to a Random Forest classifier flagging overlap with a student's home curriculum, evaluated on Eindhoven University of Technology's CS program and six approved Lund University international programs against administrator decisions. The abstract reports no accuracy figures but concludes the approach effectively identifies overlapping courses and supports curriculum alignment.

tail.title: Counterfactual Analysis via Large Language Models
tail.summary: Using GPT-3.5, they perform counterfactual analysis of return on investment under alternative interest rate schemes in online lending, first benchmarking predictive performance against gradient-boosted regression and other ML algorithms. Prompt engineering raised GPT's R-squared from 1.97% to 2.84%, approaching gradient-boosted regression's 3.48%, and GPT then generated counterfactual ROIs across alternative rates while showing logical coherence and causal reasoning in its outputs.

tail.title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Runtime for Long-Horizon Reasoning
tail.summary: Argus is a persistent, self-evolving agentic runtime with Manager, Planner, Engineer, and Reviewer roles executing bounded missions over durable project state, evaluated across seven GPT-5.5 benchmark arenas. It scores about 78% on SWE-Bench Pro versus 59% for Direct Copilot at 1.41x the token cost, and after verification-gated self-evolution, mature waves use 21% fewer solve-input tokens and 15% less workflow time than startup waves, with 34 verifier recoveries and 22 review-loop rescues.

tail.title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment
tail.summary: ABSeeker trains long-horizon search agents using Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment, which traces the ground-truth answer back to recover intermediate clues and scores each search step against them to convert sparse trajectory outcomes into dense step-level rewards for SFT and GRPO, trained on Qwen3.5-4B with only 8.5k examples. It reaches 37.3% on BrowseComp and 39.1% on BrowseComp-ZH, rising to 55.3% and 52.9% with context management, outperforming same-scale 4B agents and matching roughly 30B-parameter models.

tail.title: Otter: A Time-Aware, History-Conditioned Human Chess AI
tail.summary: Otter is a 15.3M-parameter human chess move predictor combining a 20-move history encoder with a time control module, trained on 6.1 billion positions from 117 million Lichess rapid games over 30 days on a single T4 GPU. It reaches 55.23% top-1 and 90.95% top-5 move accuracy, surpassing the prior state-of-the-art Maia 2 despite far fewer parameters and less data, with accuracy peaking at 57.38% in the 1900-1999 Elo bracket across 11 tested brackets.

tail.title: Improving Auto-Design of Neural PDE Solvers with a Domain-Specific Language
tail.summary: ADSL-PDE introduces a domain-specific language sitting between neural PDE solver concepts and executable code, representing architecture, physical constraints, objectives, sampling, and optimization choices, with a deterministic compiler generating solvers so an evolutionary agent can search over design decisions rather than raw code. Across multiple PDE benchmarks it improves both search efficiency and optimization stability, achieving more than a 52% improvement within just the first ten evolution iterations.

tail.title: From Precision Medicine to Precision Education: A Vision for AI-Powered Student Digital Twins, Preventive Student Success, and Career-Aligned Academic Pathways
tail.summary: This is a vision paper proposing Precision Education, modeled on precision medicine's shift to preventive care, in which AI continuously analyzes academic, behavioral, financial, and career data to build a Student Digital Twin that simulates educational futures and recommends interventions, grounded in early deployments like Course Signals at Purdue and GPS Advising at Georgia State. It reports no new experimental results but argues prediction alone is insufficient without a shift to causal, actionable intervention.

tail.title: A Vision for the Future of an AI-Integrated Research Ecosystem
tail.summary: This is a position paper on how generative AI is reshaping the research lifecycle, arguing that ACM-style authorship and disclosure policies, while necessary, risk obscuring deeper strains in the publication system. Drawing on the authors' experience as authors, reviewers, and readers, it sketches two contrasting visions of 2036 around four questions, the purpose of papers, reviews, human reviewers, and incentives, and closes with three grand challenges rather than any empirical findings.

tail.title: Exploring Fraction Comprehension and Interest in Elementary Education Through AI-Powered Personalized Learning
tail.summary: This dissertation includes a systematic review of AI in mathematics education (2020-2024) and a quasi-experimental study using repeated measures ANOVA to compare Mathbot, a chatbot-based personalized learning platform, against business-as-usual instruction on elementary fraction comprehension and situational interest. Mathbot produced modest improvements in fraction comprehension relative to traditional instruction, but changes in situational interest were not statistically significant, and teacher decision-making remained central to outcomes.

tail.title: Cleo: A Transparent and Controllable Chatbot for Conversational Commerce
tail.summary: Cleo is a demonstrated conversational product advisor with a hybrid architecture that separates a deterministic ranker, applying categorical filters and numeric loss functions over 3,638 product specifications, from a constrained LLM that generates descriptions grounded only in catalog evidence, plus per-attribute loss explanations and AI-generated comparisons. The paper is a system demo rather than a controlled evaluation, so no accuracy or user-study numbers are reported beyond the 3,638-item catalog size.

tail.title: Reference-Based Manipulation: A Framework and Pipeline for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
tail.summary: They run a Wizard-of-Oz study of unconstrained speech-plus-gesture input during VR scene construction to observe how users build spatial references, then formalize a framework decomposing each reference into Source, Anchor, and Frame components and characterizing their compositional strategies and explicitness. They demonstrate the framework's utility with an LLM-based pipeline implementing example interaction techniques and a preliminary technical evaluation, though the abstract reports no quantitative results.

tail.title: Posture and Sustainment Optimization Under Adversarial Uncertainty
tail.summary: They build a scenario-weighted Composite Expected Value (CEV) optimizer and an adversary-adaptive RobustCEV extension for military asset posture planning, tested across three experiments in an Indo-Pacific basing scenario with 20 assets and 5 theater locations. The greedy baseline suffers a 25.1% permanent efficiency penalty and 57.3% readiness collapse under adversarial threat; CEV recovers up to 19.8% efficiency, while RobustCEV recovers up to 158% relative to a naive optimizer against a deceptive adversary.

tail.title: TAU-Bench: From Anomaly Instance Tracking to Fine-Grained Video Anomaly Understanding
tail.summary: TAU-Bench is a track-centric benchmark for jointly evaluating anomaly instance tracking and fine-grained video anomaly understanding, containing 1,118 videos, 1,454 tracks, and 202,438 pixel-level masks across 49 event and 45 scene categories, built via an automated data engine with human quality control. Evaluating representative vision-language model families shows that models producing plausible anomaly interpretations can still fail to reliably localize and track the correct instance, revealing a persistent gap between semantic reasoning and visual grounding.

tail.title: EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
tail.summary: They study harness policy learning for long-horizon LLM agents and introduce EvoHarness-RL, which learns to construct and access external Belief, Progress, and Experience state via supervised harness fine-tuning plus cost-aware GRPO, tested on ALFWorld with a Qwen3-8B model. EvoHarness-RL reaches 96.9% success, and training shifts the agent from frequent harness calls toward selective access (harness annealing) while consolidating state into a compact, task-adaptive substrate (harness evolution).

tail.title: A Multi-Layer System for Ultra-High-Resolution Static 360-Degree Telepresence
tail.summary: They build a three-layer static 360-degree telepresence system combining an 8K panoramic camera with a rotatable 4K pan-tilt-zoom camera: a tile-based ultra-high-resolution background, a real-time foreground compositing layer via background matting, and a streamed 4K region-of-interest layer that also updates background tiles over time. They evaluate against video super-resolution baselines and run a user study on perceived detail and immersion; the abstract reports no numeric results, only that tile-based refinement with user-guided updates balances fidelity and interactivity better than the baselines.

tail.title: Sparse Mutual Information Graph Averaging for Improving Random Indexing Embeddings
tail.summary: They test whether weighted averaging on a sparse Positive Pointwise Mutual Information graph can repair weak Random Indexing (RI) word embeddings, evaluated on a fairytales corpus using a 272-question Google family-category analogy subset, plus text8 and SimLex-999, against PPMI+SVD, Binary+SVD, CBOW, Skip-gram, and Bloom filter sketches. PPMI top-K=50 graph averaging raises RI accuracy on the family subset from 19.4+-0.7% to 30.7+-2.9% across five seeds (best seed 34.6%), but the same averaging reduces accuracy for the four neural/SVD baselines and gives near-zero correlation on SimLex-999.

tail.title: DASH: Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons for On-Policy Self-Distillation of Reasoning Models
tail.summary: They address on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for RLVR reasoning models, where standard OPSD weights every local teacher-student divergence equally regardless of position or discrepancy history. DASH instead maps each local divergence's gap from the sequence-level mean to an adaptive propagation gate controlling backward multi-step aggregation, reusing the same teacher and student forward passes as OPSD. Tested on three mathematical reasoning benchmarks across three model scales, DASH improves over matched vanilla OPSD reruns on every benchmark at all three scales, with no extra inference cost; no specific percentage deltas are given.

tail.title: TS-RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Time Series Forecasting
tail.summary: They propose TS-RAG, which applies retrieval-augmented generation to time series forecasting by introducing reference tokens that fuse the input sequence with retrieved similar sequences, addressing the fact that simply concatenating retrieved sequences into prompts, as done for LLMs, does not work well for smaller time-series models. Evaluated across several real-world forecasting benchmarks, TS-RAG achieves consistent state-of-the-art performance; the abstract does not report specific accuracy, error, or effect-size numbers, only comparative superiority over unspecified baselines.

tail.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
tail.summary: They introduce EnvACE, which trains LLM tool-use agents by having the policy alternate between acting and rehearsing, generating a tool call then playing the environment role to produce the induced response, jointly optimized end-to-end with task-success rewards, removing the need for real or synthesized executable environments. Tested on BFCL-v4, tau^2-Bench, VitaBench, and FinMCP-Bench, EnvACE outperforms environment-scaling baselines overall, with rehearsal improving learning across model scales and test-time rehearsal yielding further gains under a moderate budget; no specific numeric scores are given.

tail.title: iARCS: Iterative Agentic RL for Controllable 3D Scene Generation
tail.summary: They present iARCS, an iterative agentic RL framework that adapts a pretrained 3D scene generator to natural-language task constraints via two stages: universal-reward pretraining for physical plausibility and layout quality, then task-specific fine-tuning with LLM-generated reward programs iteratively refined from training feedback. Experiments show improved constraint fidelity on walkability, reachability, and clearance-focused tasks, effective task-specific optimization, and competitive scene diversity relative to unspecified baselines; iARCS-generated data also improves a base generator, though the abstract reports no specific numeric results.

tail.title: FinEvo-Bench: A Longitudinal Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents in Professional Financial Workflows
tail.summary: FinEvo-Bench is a longitudinal benchmark of 120 real-case tasks across 20 business scenes in six financial domains, comparing four self-evolving agent scaffolds, including Letta and Codex, on a shared Qwen3.7-Max backbone against paired non-evolving controls, scored by a Claude Opus 4.6 judge. Letta reaches the highest evolved score, 91.65, and fewest compliance issues, 0.09 per task; Codex shows the largest self-evolution gain, +19.37. Evolving conditions raise scores 9.33 to 19.37 points and cut compliance issues 0.12 to 0.44 per task versus controls, with later within-scene cases outscoring early ones by 6.10 to 8.70 points.

tail.title: Training a Conditioned Video Game Agent on a VLM Annotated Dataset
tail.summary: They annotate a video game dataset with vision language models (VLMs) instructed to extract human-defined rewards, avoiding the need for game-engine access to compute RL reward signals. Offline RL is then used to train a conditioned agent that responds to desired target returns. The abstract reports no quantitative results, presenting only early experiments and a discussion of the difficulties and limitations encountered, framed as a proof-of-concept alternative to standard sparse-reward game-engine RL.

tail.title: ViSR-KGC: Visual Subgraph Reasoning with Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion
tail.summary: They propose ViSR-KGC for multimodal knowledge graph completion, which extracts a compact query-aware subgraph using learned multimodal embeddings, renders it as a visually interpretable image via an empirically selected layout strategy, and combines that image with entity images, textual descriptions, and candidate answers in a unified prompt so a vision-language model can infer the missing entity. This integrates global topology, local multimodal evidence, and VLM commonsense knowledge; the abstract reports no quantitative benchmark results or comparison numbers.

tail.title: ChainClaw: A Layered Agent Framework for Reliable On-Chain Execution
tail.summary: They present ChainClaw, a blockchain-native LLM agent framework built on OpenClaw with a layered architecture, an event-driven orchestration layer, a simulation-based safety layer with transaction simulation and action guards, and an on-chain monitoring runtime, unified by cross-layer memory, designed to address reactivity, irreversibility, and observability gaps in stateful, adversarial, economically irreversible on-chain execution. Evaluated on a purpose-built benchmark of seven tasks across four categories and five dimensions, ChainClaw consistently outperforms representative baselines on both safety and task completion; no specific numeric scores are given.

tail.title: BlockPython: A Process-Aware Agent-Supported Platform for the Transition from Block-Based to Python Programming
tail.summary: This is a system-design report describing BlockPython, a process-aware platform for transitioning learners from block-based to Python programming through bidirectional block-Python translation and four stages: Task Decomposition, Block-Based Practice, Code Challenge, and Extended Interaction. It continuously logs block artifacts, code versions, run outcomes, support use, and dialogue, combining a rule-based system for execution and stage control with an LLM-based learning assistant that gives explanations and prompts from that evidence. No evaluation numbers or empirical results are reported; it is a design and architecture description rather than a study.

tail.title: RA-CAD: Learning Post-Execution Critique for State-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation
tail.summary: They present RA-CAD, a state-aware ReAct-style agent for text-to-CAD generation that runs a Generate-Execute-Critique-Rewrite loop, first pretraining CAD coding via supervised fine-tuning (CCB), then applying trajectory-level Group Relative Policy Optimization over both code and critique sequences using terminal F1 and Chamfer Distance rewards (FAO). On CADFusion and Text2CAD, RA-CAD achieves state-of-the-art execution validity and geometric quality compared with existing methods and strong proprietary language models; the abstract does not give specific numeric scores.

tail.title: A Unified Framework for Trajectory Prediction with Explicit Planning and Reaction Decomposition
tail.summary: They propose INTraJ, a trajectory prediction framework that decomposes social influence into a planning stage, which builds reference trajectories from future social information, and a reaction stage, which recovers local adjustments from the residual between full-context prediction and that reference, supporting both multi-target and single-target settings. Tested on Argoverse 2, Argoverse 2-ped, ETH/UCY, and SDD, INTraJ gives consistent improvements, particularly in FDE and long-horizon consistency, reaching state-of-the-art performance in several settings; the abstract does not report specific numeric deltas.

tail.title: SCP-NL2TL: Selective Conformal Prediction with Semantic Verification for Natural Language to Temporal Logic Specifications
tail.summary: They propose a selective conformal prediction framework for translating natural language instructions into formal temporal-logic specifications (STL, LTL, SpaTiaL) for robots, scoring reliability via two black-box signals, back-translation fidelity and dispersion across repeated translations under semantic equivalence, then calibrating an accept-or-abstain decision with conformal risk control that gives a distribution-free bound on accepting incorrect specifications, plus a conformal anomaly detector to screen out-of-distribution inputs. Experiments across the three logic languages show improved translation reliability, robustness under tested cross-tier shifts, and effective abstention, though the abstract reports no specific numeric results.

tail.title: DoctorAgents: an agentic framework to iteratively refine AutoML pipeline for small clinical temporal data
tail.summary: They propose DoctorAgents, an agentic AutoML framework for small, temporal clinical datasets that replaces brute-force pipeline search with reasoning-driven refinement, using specialized LLM agents for generation, validation, and refinement that backpropagate natural-language feedback through textual gradient descent for targeted pipeline updates. Across diverse clinical tasks, DoctorAgents consistently outperforms established AutoML baselines while producing more interpretable task-specific representations; the abstract reports no specific accuracy or performance numbers, only comparative superiority over the baselines tested.

tail.title: Hierarchical Graph Memory for LLM Agents with Path-level Localization and Rewrite
tail.summary: They propose HiGram, a hierarchical graph memory framework for long-term LLM agent reasoning that organizes memory into coarse upper-level nodes and fine-grained MemoryUnits rather than one flat graph, uses query- and update-conditioned MicroGraphs for path-level localization of evidence before editing, and coordinates rewrites across intra-unit content and inter-unit dependencies. On long-term conversational QA and conflict-aware memory benchmarks, HiGram shows substantial improvements over baselines in answer quality and token efficiency, and improves answer accuracy and query-valid evidence selection under dynamic, static, and conditional conflicts; the abstract gives no specific numeric values.

tail.title: WorldClaw: Agentic 3D Open-World Generation at Scale
tail.summary: WorldClaw is an agentic coarse-to-fine framework where planning agents turn a text prompt into a structured spec of regions, terrain, assets, and materials, then build terrain, generate terrain-conditioned local content, reconstruct editable textured meshes, and refine placement with render-based agents. Evaluated qualitatively across diverse open-world prompts, it produces coherent, editable scenes, but the abstract reports no quantitative metrics.

tail.title: Search2Skill: Skill Distillation Beyond Knowledge Boundaries Via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
tail.summary: Search2Skill identifies an LLM agent's capability gaps, searches external sources to fill them, and distills the evidence into reusable skills, trained via rubric-based reinforcement learning that jointly optimizes when and how to search and how to generate skills. Tested on eight expert-level domains across three benchmarks, it consistently beats search-augmented and trajectory-based baselines under streaming and held-out protocols; gains come from skill abstraction, not raw retrieved evidence, and transfer across model scales.

tail.title: Coherence-Oriented Dream Scene Visualisation
tail.summary: The Dream Scene Visualiser (DSV) uses an LLM to split written dream descriptions into four chronological parts, then a text-to-image model generates a coherent four-panel sequence, regenerating any panel that mismatches its text. Evaluated on 50 dream descriptions from DreamBank using CLIP, DINOv2, and Qwen2-VL as objective quality, fidelity, and coherence measures, though the abstract reports no specific scores from this evaluation.

tail.title: NSF-HRPT: Neural Semantic Field meets Hierarchical Risk Perception Tree for Safety-Critical Scenario Assessment
tail.summary: NSF-HRPT pairs a Neural Semantic Field, trained on simulation data to model scene semantics and probabilistic time-to-collision distributions, with a Hierarchical Risk Perception Tree for parallel spatial risk reasoning from monocular video, plus a Sim2Real strategy using foundation-model priors without retraining. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on synthetic benchmarks and near-state-of-the-art results on real-world datasets for TTC estimation and risk localization, though no specific numbers are given.

tail.title: When Prompts Become Pixels: Prompt-Region Grounding for Multimodal Reasoning
tail.summary: The authors test Visualized Task Semantics (VTS), moving benchmark questions into the image while holding the underlying problem and answer fixed, across six MLLMs and four benchmarks. Accuracy drops in all 24 model-task pairs, by 17.8 points on average, since models often transcribe the visual question correctly but fail to use it. Their prompt-region grounding method raises four-benchmark VTS accuracy from 58.0 to 66.3 at matched training cost.

tail.title: Project2Task: Graph-Guided Project-Level Planning for Autonomous Research
tail.summary: Project2Task represents candidate research contributions as innovation atoms in a directed lineage graph, uses a Bernoulli block-model objective to choose horizontal, vertical, or hybrid task decompositions, and emits dependency-aware task contracts. On ten project briefs yielding roughly 30 tasks, manuscript-based evaluation gives it a quality score of 7.15 versus 4.58 for a Brief Baseline and 5.31 for Topic-only; pairing its contracts with AutoResearchClaw raises downstream task accuracy from 0.536 to 0.759.

tail.title: Traceable LLM-Generated Hazard Scenarios for Operational Safety Analysis of Aviation Systems Using ASRS Reports
tail.summary: The authors generate candidate aviation hazard scenarios from NASA's ASRS reports, producing structured categorical-factor hypotheses plus narrative event sequences, each scored for plausibility via historical co-occurrence and traced to similar held-out reports; a hybrid variant conditions narratives on hypotheses from evolutionary abduction. They evaluate multiple LLMs under zero-shot versus few-shot prompting and optional fine-tuning for validity and realism, but the abstract reports no specific accuracy numbers.

tail.title: When Privileged Guidance Misaligns: State-Matched Routing and Contextualized Self-Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
tail.summary: SMRC-SD addresses state-reference mismatch in privileged on-policy distillation for multi-turn LLM agents by checking, at each turn, whether the student's execution state matches a supported state along a reference trajectory, distilling only at matched states with state-conditioned teacher context. With Qwen3-1.7B on ALFWorld and WebShop, it beats unconditional full-path distillation, raising task success from 0.746 to 0.865 on ALFWorld and 0.574 to 0.693 on WebShop.

tail.title: Abstract Event Causal Rules: Induction and Application
tail.summary: The authors propose Abstract Event Causal Rules (AECR), converting concrete cause-effect pairs into generalized abstract causal logic via a multi-agent Concrete-to-Abstract Causal Induction system with similarity-constrained clustering, building two AECR knowledge bases from noisy raw data. Injecting AECRs into a Graph Event Prediction benchmark through rule-guided attention and gated fusion substantially strengthens generalization and yields consistent prediction gains, largest on rare and unseen events, though no specific numbers are reported.

tail.title: CARGO-VL: Counterfactual Arbitration with Risk-Constrained Group Optimization for Vision-Language Models
tail.summary: CARGO-VL is a group-relative post-training framework for vision-language models that jointly optimizes matched variants across four evidence conditions (aligned, image-correct, text-correct, both-wrong), combining condition-wise correctness with transition rewards for answer invariance, source equivariance, and abstention switching under a primal-dual risk controller. Tested on their new XMC resource plus CMC-Bench and Modality-Bias across multiple seeds, it improves conflict handling, unsupported-answer avoidance, and modality balance over pointwise baselines, though no score deltas are given.

tail.title: Architectural Implications of Agentic AI Workflows
tail.summary: The authors characterize agentic AI workflows architecturally through a production study at Microsoft Azure plus a controlled study of open-source frameworks, showing execution fragments into LLM inferences, tool calls, and orchestration that repeatedly cross the CPU-GPU boundary under bursty, low-average load. Their Agora prototype dynamically harvests idle CPU cores, oversubscribes GPU memory with state prefetching, and applies role-based, affinity-aware scheduling, improving utilization and throughput while preserving tail latency, though no specific numbers are given.

tail.title: Non-asymptotic implicit bias of logistic regression at early-stage gradient descent dynamics
tail.summary: This theoretical paper examines why gradient descent on logistic regression aligns with the max-margin direction well before the slow asymptotic rate previously established for exponentially tailed losses. Tracking radial and tangential flow components against dataset geometry rather than asymptotic expansion, the authors prove weak alignment with the max-margin direction occurs within O(exp(exp(-delta))) iterations for permissible alignment error delta, and show this bound is tight.

tail.title: GAUGE: A Measurement-Grounded Benchmark for Physical Fidelity in Simulation Engines and Video World Models
tail.summary: GAUGE is a real-world-grounded benchmark with 22 controlled task families spanning rigid bodies, cables, textiles, and deformable objects, used to jointly test physics engines and generative video world models. Benchmarking Isaac Sim, Genesis, and Newton on 14 task families via trajectory errors, and 6 image-to-video models on 5 rigid-body tasks, they find no uniformly faithful engine, with worst errors in impulsive contact and deformation, and video models matching equation form but recovering wrong accelerations.

tail.title: PD-GS: Phoneme-Driven 3DGS for Audio-Driven Talking Heads
tail.summary: PD-GS augments a 3D Gaussian Splatting talking-head model with time-aligned phoneme tokens from an ASR and forced-alignment pipeline, fused with continuous audio embeddings via a learned-gate Linguistic Fusion Module to counter the over-smoothed, regression-biased mouth motion causing the leaky-mouth artifact, training purely from monocular video. On HDTF, PD-GS achieves the best lip geometry among baselines with a landmark distance of 2.66 and qualitatively reduces closure violations on hard phoneme sequences.

tail.title: EndoVLM: An Endoscopy Vision-Language Pre-training Model via Anatomy-Guided Sparsity and Progressive Alignment
tail.summary: EndoVLM is a vision-language foundation model pre-trained on over 348,000 endoscopic examinations pairing clinical reports with image collections, using Anatomy-Guided Sparse Pooling to aggregate salient frames, Progressive Semantic-Aware Alignment for patient-level to fine-grained anatomical matching, and a Semantic-Concentrated Masked Autoencoder on those frames. Across downstream tasks it outperforms existing foundation models, stays competitive with task-specific methods, and shows robust zero-shot generalization, though the abstract gives no specific numeric scores.

tail.title: Design and Evaluation of a Touchscreen-Based Teleoperation Interface for Robotic Manipulators
tail.summary: The authors built a touchscreen teleoperation interface mapping finger movements to a Franka Emika Panda arm for nuclear surface-contact tasks, and ran a 20-participant study against a joystick and a single-click autonomous mode, remotely controlling the arm from another country. The touchscreen cut completion time by 53.5% (2.50 vs 5.38 min median), raised path coverage to 90.7% vs 84.1%, and lowered NASA-TLX load from 52 to 43 (-17.3%); the autonomous mode was lowest at 31.

tail.title: SkillTFM: Gated Skill Evolution for Training-Free Adaptation of Tabular Foundation Models
tail.summary: SkillTFM is a training-free adaptation system for tabular foundation models that replaces parameter updates with gated evolution of agentic skills, using a verifiable skill bank that identifies boundary evidence characterizing task structure and base-model failures, then retrieves and extends skills subject to validation. Across simulated boundary settings and real-world electricity-price forecasting, SkillTFM improves AUC by 0.128 to 0.142 and raises nonlinear-boundary AUC from 0.699 to 0.898, with generality confirmed across multiple TFM backbones.

tail.title: Macaw - a 2.6B on-device macOS agent with 97 hand-written tools, 1.5 GB in 4-bit MLX
tail.summary: Bad Theory Labs fine-tuned LiquidAI's LFM2.5-2.6B into a local macOS assistant that chains multi-step actions (send an email, find a file, read a PDF, report what is draining the battery) across 97 hand-written and tested tools. The 4-bit MLX build is 1.5 GB, runs in about 2 GB of memory, and answers in roughly a second on an M2; it serves an OpenAI-compatible endpoint via mlx_lm.server so you can pass your own tool schemas. Everything stays on the machine with no account required.

tail.title: A 304B DeepSeek V4 Flash running in 6.5 GB of RAM by streaming experts off SSD
tail.summary: An mlx-optiq 2-bit mixed-precision quant of DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731: 608 GB at bf16 becomes 92.5 GB on disk, but only about 6.5 GB stays resident while generating because attention, the router, the shared expert and embeddings stay in RAM and the 256 routed experts are read off SSD as the router selects them. The card offers qualitative evidence rather than benchmarks - the 2-bit model chained two rules of a 928-token job-queue spec correctly and wrote a working Flappy Bird in one HTML file - and publishes no capability score, which is an honest gap rather than a hidden one.

tail.title: Ornith-1.0-35B quantized to 27 GB with the vision tower kept at bf16 in a sidecar
tail.summary: A 6-bit mixed-precision MLX quant of deep-reinforce's Ornith-1.0-35B (a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-architecture sparse MoE), taking 70.2 GB of bf16 weights to 27 GB with 448 sensitive layers held at 8-bit and 63 robust ones dropped to 4-bit. Notably the vision tower is preserved at bf16 in a separate sidecar file, so unlike most aggressive quants this one still accepts image input. A 9B sibling quant shipped the day before.

tail.title: Ornith-1.0-9B gets a 6-bit OptiQ quant alongside the 35B
tail.summary: The dense 9B member of deep-reinforce's Ornith-1.0 agentic-coding family, quantized to 6-bit mixed precision for Apple Silicon. Ornith-1.0 is the MIT-licensed family (9B dense, 31B dense, 35B MoE, 397B MoE, post-trained on Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5) whose selling point is an RL framework that learns the agent scaffold jointly with the solution rollouts. Ornith-1.0-35B is also the base that Bad Theory Labs' BTL-4 was fine-tuned from this week.

tail.title: tiny-pickle-v3-coder - a small coder model shipped with base, LoRA, GGUF and MLX on day one
tail.summary: vsan released tiny-pickle-v3-coder as a full set (weights, the LoRA used to make it, and GGUF), with an mlx-community 4-bit conversion following the same day; the config identifies a qwen3_moe backbone tagged for coding and software engineering. It follows tiny-pickle-35b from two days earlier. The base repo currently returns 401 through the HF API, so weights are reachable via the derivative repos but the canonical card is not publicly inspectable - worth noting before trusting any claim about it.

tail.title: Nanbeige4.2-3B ships FP8 and GPTQ-Int8 builds of its looped-transformer agentic 3B
tail.summary: Nanbeige published FP8 and GPTQ-Int8 quantizations of Nanbeige4.2-3B, a compact agentic model whose Looped Transformer architecture reuses transformer layers to buy capacity without adding parameters - the same trick min-spark applies three orders of magnitude smaller. Only 3B non-embedding parameters, trained with environment-synthesis SFT plus RL combining outcome and process rewards. Technical report is arXiv 2607.22083.

tail.title: Kimi-K3-Abliterated - refusal removal applied to a 2.8T-parameter frontier open-weight model
tail.summary: SHS-Lab published a compressed-tensors abliteration of Moonshot's Kimi-K3, the 2.8T-parameter multimodal MoE. Abliterating a model at this scale is a different proposition from doing it to a 2.6B edge model, and it lands the same week that SGLang and Unsloth both shipped day-0 K3 serving support - the open-weight frontier and its safety-stripped derivative arriving essentially together.

tail.title: AMD publishes a W8A8 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B for EPYC CPU inference through ZenDNN
tail.summary: AMD quantized Qwen3.6-35B-A3B to 8-bit weights with 8-bit dynamic activations using vLLM's LLM Compressor v0.12.0, targeting CPU-only inference on EPYC through the ZenDNN v6.1.0 / ZenTorch stack with vLLM v0.26.0. It is a reminder that the MoE-on-CPU path is being productized by a chip vendor, not just hobbyists - and that the compressed-tensors format is now the common currency between the GPU and CPU serving stacks.

tail.title: lattice-retrieval embeds all 6.4M English Wikipedia articles in 7 minutes 26 seconds on a MacBook Air
tail.summary: A static English retrieval embedding model that is literally just a 30,522 x 1,024 token embedding table with mean pooling - no transformer layers, no attention, no contextual representations - paired with a pure-Rust runtime that embeds the full English Wikipedia in 7m26s on an 8-core M2 MacBook Air. Pretrained on ~660M query/document pairs then fine-tuned with hard negatives, it scores 0.0415 higher on decontaminated BEIR NDCG@10 than the previous best static embedding model, on roughly eight times the training data.

tail.title: A reranker trained on peer-review-to-paper pairs cuts its base model's error rate 57%
tail.summary: A gte-reranker-modernbert cross-encoder fine-tuned on an unusual supervision signal: the query is a peer reviewer's own summary of a paper, written by a domain expert, and the positive is the paper that review is attached to - not a heuristic, not a click, not LLM-generated. On 3,157 held-out queries over 1,534 paper-disjoint papers with 8 mined hard negatives each, it reports P@1 0.9290 versus 0.8334 for the base model at 41 ms/query. The eval design (paper-disjoint splits, explicit random-chance baseline of 0.1111) is unusually well specified for a community upload.

tail.title: Tianmu-Emb-Uni-8B - a unified text/image/audio/video embedding model on a Qwen3-VL backbone
tail.summary: An 8B unified multimodal embedding model with 3584-dimensional output, built on Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B with an audio branch initialized from the Qwen2.5-Omni audio tower and connected through a trained adapter. Worth reading the fine print: the released checkpoint is a stage1b adapter/prototype stage, it ships only the trained audio-side modules, connector, projection and prototype weights rather than full base weights, and it does not support AutoModel.from_pretrained - so 'released' here does not mean drop-in.

tail.title: Paprika - the most accurate freely available Lithuanian ASR, at 16.98% WER
tail.summary: A whisper-large-v3-turbo fine-tune for Lithuanian, warm-started from an existing community model and trained 8,000 steps on ~320 hours (LIEPA-3 spontaneous and read speech plus VoxPopuli LT), with benchmark speakers excluded from training. It reports 16.98% WER / 10.01% CER on held-out VoxPopuli LT against 18.13% for its own base and 30.03% for stock whisper-large-v3-turbo, plus a same-harness FLEURS-lt comparison measured 2026-08-07. RTF around 0.10 with MLX on Apple Silicon.

tail.title: Rose-Medium - 97.82M parameters, 80B tokens, and a model card that admits disappointment
tail.summary: A ~97.82M-parameter custom-architecture (Rose X1) causal LM trained on approximately 80.06B tokens with a native 2048-token context. The card is unusual for openly framing the result as below the author's expectations and flagging specific benchmark anomalies (ARC-Easy) instead of claiming a win - a rare instance of a community release publishing its own confusion rather than smoothing it over.

tail.title: LeRobot ships a native EO-1 vision-language-action policy checkpoint
tail.summary: A lossless key-layout conversion of IPEC-COMMUNITY/EO-1-3B into LeRobot's native eo1 policy implementation, preserving the released Qwen vision-language weights, LM head, state/action projectors and flow-matching head. Release defaults are carried over: action chunk size 16, max state/action dimension 32, two action-projector layers, ten denoising steps. Usable directly with --policy.path=lerobot/eo1-base for training or rollout.

tail.title: Renesas is porting NVIDIA's Alpamayo1.5-10B driving VLA to R-Car Gen5 silicon
tail.summary: Renesas opened a repo for an optimized deployment of NVIDIA's Alpamayo-1.5-10B autonomous-driving VLA - a Cosmos-Reason2 8.2B VLM backbone plus a 2.3B diffusion trajectory decoder, taking four-camera 10Hz video, text navigation commands and egomotion history, and emitting chain-of-thought driving rationale plus a 6.4-second trajectory. The repo is explicitly tagged 'coming soon' with no weights and no release date, so this is a stated intention rather than a shipped model.

tail.title: Faster-WAM releases checkpoints for inference-time future conditioning in world action models
tail.summary: Official LIBERO and RoboTwin checkpoints for Faster-WAM (arXiv 2608.04404), which makes world action models robust by conditioning on predicted futures at inference time rather than paying for it during training. Ships the dataset statistics files the evaluation pipelines require, so the results are reproducible rather than checkpoint-only.

tail.title: W2-VLA conditions robot manipulation on predicted future wrist views
tail.summary: Official LIBERO checkpoints for World-to-Wrist (arXiv 2608.05369), a vision-language-action model built on Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct with V-JEPA2, which predicts what the wrist camera will see next as a task-conditioned auxiliary signal for fine-grained manipulation. Training data is published alongside the weights.

tail.title: UA-NWM releases an uncertainty-aware world model for aerial image-goal navigation
tail.summary: Checkpoints for UA-NWM (arXiv 2608.05597), which pairs a shared deterministic backbone with a hypothesis-entropy module so an aerial navigation policy can score its own uncertainty rather than committing to a single latent prediction. One checkpoint serves both the uncertainty-aware scoring path and the deterministic DINOv3-cosine baseline, which makes the ablation honest. The DINOv3 encoder itself is not redistributed.

tail.title: Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B arrives in Diffusers format with a distilled sibling
tail.summary: Wan-AI published Diffusers-format conversions of Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B and a distilled variant, using a new WanAnimate2Pipeline class, which lands the same week ComfyUI v0.31.0 added Wan-Animate2 support. The model cards themselves are empty ModelScope stubs with no description - weights first, documentation later.

tail.title: NVIDIA's Qwen-Image-Flash gets GGUF quantizations for ComfyUI
tail.summary: GGUF quantizations of nvidia/Qwen-Image-Flash, the DMD2-distilled few-step version of Qwen-Image released under the NVIDIA Open Model License, packaged for ComfyUI. Few-step distillation plus GGUF quantization is the combination that has been moving image generation onto mid-range cards this quarter.

tail.title: A Krea-2 LoRA that generates coherent 8-panel cinematic storyboards
tail.summary: A LoRA on krea/Krea-2-Raw trained to produce eight-panel storyboards from character, environment and visual references, with deliberate shot-to-shot changes in camera framing, perspective and character performance rather than a static grid layout. It is a small example of the sequential-consistency problem being attacked with a LoRA instead of a video model.

tail.title: AMD publishes whisper-large-v3-turbo compiled for its NPU via ONNX
tail.summary: An ONNX build of whisper-large-v3-turbo targeted at AMD's on-die NPU rather than GPU or CPU. The repo has no README yet, so there are no published latency or accuracy numbers to check - the artifact exists but the claim does not, which is worth waiting out before treating it as a usable NPU speech path.

tail.title: BigBang-V1 now has an inspectable model card and community GGUFs - the corroboration gap has closed
tail.summary: BigBang-V1, previously flagged here as an uncorroborated leaderboard entry, now has a full public model card on endless-frontier/BigBang-v1 with a stated method and inspectable weights, plus bartowski GGUF conversions as of 2026-08-07. The method is specific enough to argue with: an adversarial self-evolving loop where generator agents propose verifiable frontier problems and critic agents score correctness, difficulty, scalability and diversity, yielding only ~10,000 post-training examples on top of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. The claim is that this places aggregate performance between DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B) and V4 Pro - still lab-reported, but now checkable.

tail.title: Maple-Preview's ternary GGUF port needs a llama.cpp fork mainline cannot load
tail.summary: GGUF conversions of DeepGrove's Maple-Preview, a 20B-A1B ternary-weight MoE reasoning model (5.31 GB checkpoint, 131k context, 218 tok/s claimed on an M4 Mac mini). All three packs now generate on GPU with all layers offloaded - f16 at ~385 tok/s on an H200 and tq2_0 at ~97 tok/s on an RTX 4000 Ada - but only under the stamsam/llama.cpp prism-branch fork. The card states plainly that mainline llama.cpp cannot run any of these files because the maple architecture and its ternary format exist only in the fork.

tail.title: Baseten joins Hugging Face Inference Providers
tail.summary: Hugging Face added Baseten as a routable inference provider, so models can be called through the HF Inference Providers layer against Baseten's infrastructure with billing handled through HF. For anyone routing eval pipelines by provider, it is one more backend whose throughput and pricing sit behind the same API surface.

tail.title: llama.cpp adds server tool isolation, running tool calls inside a Docker sandbox
tail.summary: Build b10328 adds initial tool-isolation support to llama-server, letting tool calls execute inside a Docker sandbox (the option was renamed from 'sandbox' to 'isolate', with x-tool-runtime replacing x-tool-docker). This is the local-serving stack growing the same containment primitive the hosted agent tools have, which matters if you are running an untrusted tool loop against a local model.

tail.title: llama.cpp fuses rms_norm + mul + rope into a single CUDA kernel path
tail.summary: Build b10330 fuses rms_norm, mul and rope (plus view/set_rows) into one CUDA kernel, with added memory-range safety checks and broadcast-weight test coverage for the fusion. Kernel fusion in the norm-plus-rope path is one of the remaining easy wins for decode throughput on consumer NVIDIA cards.

tail.title: ComfyUI v0.31.0 adds Wan-Animate2, int8 VAE quantization and MiniMax-H3 audio fixes
tail.summary: Adds Wan-Animate2 support, int8_convrot VAE quantization for MiniMax-H3, and asymmetric w4a8_int quantization, plus fixes for H3 noise-mask sampling, audio corruption under EasyCache, and full-offload on the audio VAE. Also speeds up LTX and Wan sampling and fixes memory pinning on Linux systems without swap. The int8 VAE path is the piece that matters for fitting H3 video-plus-audio into a 16GB card.

tail.title: ExLlamaV3 v1.4.1 adds Mistral-4 and switches grammar to LLGuidance
tail.summary: Adds Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration (Mistral-4) support and logit bias, and replaces Formatron with LLGuidance as the default constrained-decoding backend (Formatron stays available as an optional dependency). Filters and grammars can now be combined with banned_strings, which is the combination you want for structured-output evals.

tail.title: Sentence Transformers v5.7.0 rebuilds GradCache and fixes silent wrong-gradient bugs
tail.summary: Rebuilds every gradient-cached loss onto one shared engine, fixing several previously silent incorrect-gradient bugs, and adds token-based mini-batching for up to 3.9x faster cached-loss training; model.compile() now actually accelerates inference. Two breaking changes to note before upgrading an embedding pipeline: int8/uint8 embedding quantization now clips and floors, so output is no longer bit-identical to prior versions, and AdaptiveLayerLoss/Matryoshka2dLoss weight prior-layer losses uniformly by default.

tail.title: DeepSpeed v0.19.4 enables ZeRO-3 inference with tensor parallelism
tail.summary: Lets ZeRO stage 3 inference run with AutoTP tensor parallelism and adds AutoTP support for HuggingFace colwise_gather_output in lm_head replacement, plus universal-checkpoint metadata preservation for HF tp_plan. Also fixes MoE capacity-drop clamping, AutoEP rank-split derivation, and three learning-rate scheduler bugs including WarmupLR collapsing multiple param groups.

tail.title: huggingface_hub v1.27.0 installs an 'agent skill' for the hf CLI by default
tail.summary: The standalone hf-cli installers now install an agent skill - a bundle teaching coding agents how to use the hf CLI - globally by default, with --exclude-skill to opt out, and hf update keeps it in sync without silently reinstalling a skill you deleted. Worth noticing as a pattern: a mainstream Python SDK installer now ships agent-facing instructions into your global config as the default behaviour.

tail.title: compressed-tensors v0.18.0 fixes NVFP4 packing for float32 and speeds up offloading
tail.summary: Adds safetensors loading directly onto meta devices, several offloading fixes (explicit class patching, forced buffer offloading, a single OffloadedWeightsLoader instantiation for faster to_accelerate, better disk-offload errors), and fixes NVFP4 packing for float32 inputs with a faster lower-memory pack_fp4_to_uint8. Quantization scheme application is now restricted to Linear, Embedding and Attention layers only.

tail.title: Claude Code v2.1.225 fixes an MCP OAuth keychain failure causing 401 bursts on macOS
tail.summary: Fixes MCP OAuth servers on macOS intermittently failing with bursts of 401s after a keychain read timeout, and a transient 401 replacing a long-lived CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Adds gateway spend-limit support to the usage warning and a workspace trust prompt when running claude agents in an untrusted directory, and stops cross-session messages parking indefinitely without notice or expiry in headless sessions.

tail.title: Claude Code v2.1.226 and the TypeScript SDK reach parity
tail.summary: A maintenance release of bug fixes and reliability improvements, shipping in lockstep with claude-agent-sdk-typescript v0.3.226. Four Claude Code releases landed in three days this window (223 through 226), which is the current cadence to plan pinning around.

tail.title: Claude Agent SDK v0.3.225 fixes background subagents that never resumed
tail.summary: Fixes background subagents in headless and SDK sessions never resuming when a background shell command or Monitor they had left running completed, so the subagent never saw the result. A silent-hang class of bug worth knowing about if you have been running fan-out agent pipelines headlessly.

tail.title: Claude Agent SDK v0.3.224 adds cross-session messaging settings and fixes path collisions
tail.summary: Adds crossSessionInbound and dialogExpiry settings for cross-session SendMessage under bypassed permissions, a subkind 'peer-send-message' marker on task-notification messages, and an archive plugin source. Also fixes project paths over 200 characters colliding with another project's session directory - a quiet data-mixing bug for anyone with deep directory trees.

tail.title: Anthropic Python and TypeScript SDKs add session budgets, an advisor tool and GitHub skill auto-loading
tail.summary: Python v0.121.0 and TypeScript sdk v0.116.0 both add the mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01 beta plus session budgets, an advisor tool, pinned inference location, and skills auto-loading from GitHub. The Python SDK drops the retired Claude Opus 4.1 models; the TypeScript side shipped all six packages (sdk, vertex, bedrock, aws, google-cloud, foundry) the same day with a fix for User-Agent strings using hardcoded values instead of constructor names.

tail.title: Claude Agent SDK for Python cut four releases in three days, all CLI version bumps
tail.summary: Versions v0.2.131 through v0.2.134 shipped 2026-08-06 to 08-08, each bumping only the bundled Claude CLI to track Claude Code v2.1.223 through v2.1.226 with no Python-level API changes. Useful to know when reading the changelog: the Python SDK's version churn this week is entirely downstream of the CLI, not the library.

tail.title: MCP Inspector 2.1.0 mirrors SEP-2243 header arguments on tools/call
tail.summary: Fixes Inspector to mirror SEP-2243 x-mcp-header arguments into Mcp-Param-* headers on tools/call, aligning the reference debugging tool with the parameter-to-header mapping extension in the MCP spec. Also restores a SECURITY.md lost in the v2 repo tree swap and documents the post-swap branch and milestone policy.

tail.title: FastMCP v3.4.6 routes OAuth and JWKS fetches through a mandated trusted proxy
tail.summary: A security backport to the 3.x branch letting deployments route SSRF-protected OAuth metadata and JWKS fetches through a corporate proxy while preserving custom CA certificates. The design choice worth noting: when no trusted proxy is configured FastMCP refuses the fetch outright rather than falling back to an unprotected direct request - fail closed, not open. A 4.0.0b2 beta two days later serialized an event-store read-modify-write race.

tail.title: Pydantic AI v2.27.0 adds a Snowflake Cortex model and fixes compaction round-tripping
tail.summary: Makes CompactionPart round-trip correctly through the Vercel AI and AG-UI adapters, so context compaction survives the transport layer instead of being silently dropped. Also adds SnowflakeModel and SnowflakeProvider for Snowflake Cortex and an xai_agent_count setting; v2.25.0 two days earlier forwarded xAI FileSearchTool collection options and fixed Azure sending max_tokens instead of max_completion_tokens for Mistral models.

tail.title: MCP's stateless core lands, unblocking serverless MCP servers
tail.summary: Google walked through the 2026-07-28 MCP spec update that replaces the protocol's legacy stateful session constraints with a fully stateless core, adding new HTTP headers and multi-round-trip request support. The practical consequence is that MCP servers can now be deployed on serverless and autoscaling infrastructure without pinning a client to one instance for the life of a session.

tail.title: Qwen Code v0.21.8 fixes distrusted workspaces inheriting trust from parent directories
tail.summary: A security fix where a workspace explicitly marked as distrusted incorrectly inherited trust from its parent directory - the kind of bug that makes a trust boundary decorative. Also restores real-time autofix for PRs opened from forks, enables compression cache sharing across OpenAI/Gemini/Vertex AI, and reports /review prompt cache hit rates up to 93.3%. The prior release, v0.21.7, removed the 50-turn Goals limit and added inline terminal image rendering for Kitty, Ghostty and chafa.

tail.title: LangSmith SDK sanitizes git remote credentials before they leak into trace metadata
tail.summary: v0.10.16/v0.10.17 strip credentials embedded in git remote URLs before they can be written into trace metadata, and mask metadata after the runtime-environment merge and via the anonymizer. If you have been tracing runs from repos cloned with a token in the remote URL, those tokens may already be sitting in your trace store.

tail.title: crewAI clears seven security advisories across three releases in a week
tail.summary: Releases 1.15.11 through 1.15.13 bumped aiohttp and cryptography to clear six GHSA advisories and h2 to 4.4.1 for GHSA-6hr6-w5qg-qmwg, added a URLReadTool for reading arbitrary URLs, and unified scaffolding under crewai create. Also fixed underreporting of Anthropic cache token usage, which matters if you have been costing runs from crewAI's own numbers.

tail.title: E2B patches a high-severity undici advisory across its Python and JS SDKs
tail.summary: Bumps both undici dependencies past the 2026-07-24 advisories, fixing one High (GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272) and four Medium issues plus HTTP/2 stream-settling, retry and GOAWAY handling. Also aligns ANSI stripping of template build logs between the Python and JS SDKs and relaxes the Python wcmatch constraint for compatibility with deepagents 0.7.0 and similar.

tail.title: opencode simplifies xAI login to a device-code flow and fixes message ordering
tail.summary: v1.18.14/v1.18.15 reduce xAI login to a single device-code flow suitable for headless and remote environments, preserve structured mid-stream provider errors so compatible providers can retry, fix chronological message ordering for imported/legacy IDs and revert/fork actions, and add full session transcript export as JSON in the desktop app. Note the repo has moved to anomalyco/opencode from sst/opencode.

tail.title: OpenHands switches its Canvas default model to GLM 5.2 and adds per-run cost display
tail.summary: v1.10.0 sets GLM 5.2 as the Canvas default model, adds activity log export and a featured automations dashboard; v1.11.0 and v1.12.0 add per-run LLM cost display in the activity log and exports, and clarify which OpenHands model endpoints are free. A widely-used open agent framework defaulting to a Chinese open-weight model is itself a data point on where the price-performance line now sits.

tail.title: google-genai v2.17.0 adds the Gemini Robotics ER 2 Preview model
tail.summary: Adds the Gemini Robotics ER 2 Preview model and a TOO_MANY_TOOL_CALLS FinishReason enum value - the latter being a newly first-class failure mode worth handling in any agent loop against Gemini. Also adds propertyOrdering auto-population for response schemas and a top-level errors array on the Interaction resource.

tail.title: LangGraph checkpointers fix delta-channel history walks at plain-value seeds
tail.summary: checkpoint 4.2.0 and checkpoint-postgres 3.1.2 fix collecting writes at a plain-value seed when walking delta channel history, applied consistently across core and Postgres, and add a conformance test suite shared between the Postgres and SQLite checkpointers. Shared conformance tests are the more durable part of this.

tail.title: Agno v2.8.7 adds AdvisorTools for model-to-model feedback
tail.summary: Adds AdvisorTools, which lets an agent ask a separate advisor model for feedback mid-run, plus an OpenRouteService routing toolkit. Also fixes Cohere silently dropping zero-valued sampling parameters - a quiet correctness bug if you have been setting temperature=0 through Agno - and excludes nltk 3.10.1, which broke the unstructured import chain.

tail.title: Anthropic opens self-hosted environments for Claude Code sessions in public beta
tail.summary: Team and Enterprise organizations can now run Claude Code cloud sessions - web, mobile, desktop, terminal or scheduled - on infrastructure inside their own network instead of Anthropic's, with repo checkouts, build artifacts, secrets and session-created files staying on customer-provisioned machines. It is off by default and pairs with the claude self-hosted-runner command that shipped in CLI v2.1.224 the next day.

tail.title: Claude Enterprise adds inference hooks for inline data-loss prevention
tail.summary: An inline DLP layer that inspects prompts and outputs at inference time rather than only at ingestion, so policy violations can be caught in the response path. Part of a run of enterprise infrastructure announcements in the first week of August alongside the self-hosted Claude Code beta.

tail.title: Qwen3.8-Max is now corroborated: 2.4T total, 95B active, and an official API launch
tail.summary: Qwen3.8-Max was flagged here as an uncorroborated OpenRouter listing with no lab announcement. Alibaba has since announced it officially at WAIC Shanghai and launched the API on 2026-08-03: 2.4T total parameters with 95B active in an MoE, 1M context, priced at $2 input / $6 output / $0.25 cached per million tokens, with open weights said to follow. The OpenRouter listing prices it at $2/$6 per million, matching. Weights are still not published, so the open-weight half of the claim remains outstanding.

tail.title: Tencent makes Hy3 free worldwide through 31 August
tail.summary: Tencent broadened international access to Hy3 - a 295B-total / 21B-active hybrid MoE with 256K context and fast/slow thinking modes - making it free worldwide via WorkBuddy until 31 August and adding availability through Tencent Design Miora and Tencent Cloud TokenHub. This is a distribution change to the model that launched 6 July, not a new release; Hy3 was previously flagged here for thin corroboration and now has both weights on HuggingFace and an official company announcement.

tail.title: xAI repoints grok-voice-latest to Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0
tail.summary: The grok-voice-latest API alias began routing to grok-voice-think-fast-2.0, the speech-to-speech model announced 29 July, as of 5 August. A default-routing change rather than a launch, but the kind that silently changes what your pinned-by-alias pipeline is actually calling.

tail.title: Google Cloud API Gateway adds model routing across providers in public preview
tail.summary: API Gateway can now route requests dynamically across multiple models and providers through a single endpoint instead of hardcoded per-model integrations - Google shipping an OpenRouter-shaped abstraction inside its own cloud. Worth watching for anyone whose routing layer is currently a single point of dependency.

tail.title: oh-my-pi - a terminal coding agent using hash-anchored edits instead of line numbers
tail.summary: A terminal coding agent built around hash-anchored edits (the edit refers to a content hash, not a line number, so it cannot silently apply to the wrong place) and a deliberately trimmed tool harness. The hash-anchoring idea is the interesting part and is worth stealing conceptually even if Patrick stays on Claude Code.

tail.title: openwork - open-source alternative to Claude Cowork, built on opencode
tail.summary: An open-source alternative to Claude Cowork built on opencode, at ~2,367 stars in a day. Interesting as a look at what a self-hosted multi-agent workspace looks like when you can read every line of the orchestration.

tail.title: cc-switch - one desktop panel for switching Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode configs
tail.summary: A cross-platform desktop switcher for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode configs - swap accounts, endpoints, and provider setups without hand-editing JSON. Practical if Patrick juggles subscription vs API-key contexts across his projects.

tail.title: rtk - a CLI proxy that cuts agent token spend on shell command output
tail.summary: A CLI proxy that claims 60-90% token reduction on common dev commands by summarising and structuring tool output before it reaches the model. Given how much of Patrick's spend is agent tool-output, this is the kind of thing worth measuring on one real session.

tail.title: witr - trace any process, port, or file back to what actually started it
tail.summary: 'Why is this running?' - trace any process, port, container, or file back to the thing that spawned it. Not AI, just a genuinely good debugging tool, and the sort of question that comes up constantly when an agent has left background processes around.

tail.title: LifeOS - an open-source hill-climbing AI harness for personal goal state
tail.summary: Daniel Miessler's 'general hill-climbing AI harness' for moving from current state to desired state across life domains, now open source. Whatever you think of the framing, the structure - explicit state, explicit telemetry, agent loops over your own data - overlaps hard with what Patrick is building in his Baseline psych app.

tail.title: agent-governance-toolkit - Microsoft ships policy enforcement and audit trails for agents
tail.summary: Microsoft's toolkit for agent governance: policy enforcement, zero-trust identity for agents, and execution audit trails. This is the enterprise-compliance framing of the same problem Patrick audits academically, and it is a useful citation for how industry is operationalising agent oversight.

tail.title: skill-recorder - record your screen, get an agent skill out of it
tail.summary: A desktop app that records what you actually do on screen and turns the session into an agent skill. This is the inverse of writing SKILL.md by hand: demonstrate the workflow once, get a reusable skill. For someone with as many hand-authored skills as Patrick, the capture-by-demonstration angle is the interesting bit.

tail.title: captain-miao - herd multiple coding agents across kitty/zellij panes
tail.summary: Herds multiple coding agents inside kitty or zellij panes, giving each its own workspace and letting you watch them all at once. A terminal-native answer to the same problem the Mac orchestrators are solving.

tail.title: 49IDE - a 2D spatial grid for managing many agents, git trees, and issues at once
tail.summary: A 2D grid IDE that puts terminals, git trees, Beads issue tables, notes, and files on one spatial canvas, with multiple machines joinable over a private network. The author built it because running six-plus agents across three projects fragmented his context beyond what tabs could hold - a problem Patrick will recognise.

tail.title: A free DOCX editor with an MCP server, so agents can edit Word docs directly
tail.summary: A free DOCX editor that ships an MCP server, so an agent can open, edit, and save Word documents directly rather than round-tripping through pandoc. Immediately relevant for anyone who has to deliver client reports in .docx - which is exactly Patrick's consulting output.

tail.title: pocket-tts - a text-to-speech model that fits on your CPU
tail.summary: Kyutai's TTS small enough to run on CPU. Patrick's audio-overview skill already runs Kokoro on the GPU; a competent CPU-only TTS means narration can run without contending for VRAM while a model is loaded.

tail.title: VibeVoice - Microsoft open-sources its frontier voice model
tail.summary: Microsoft's open frontier voice model, back in the trending list at ~52k stars. Relevant to Patrick's audio pipeline as the obvious quality comparison against Kokoro for long-form narration.

tail.title: ComfyUI 0.31.1 - MiniMax H3 VAE fixes and a restored attention fast path
tail.summary: ComfyUI 0.31.0/0.31.1 hardens node combo handling, fixes MiniMax H3 VAE device casting, restores an SDPA small-attention bypass, and stops over-pinning memory on Linux systems without swap. Routine but worth taking if Patrick is running the H3 video nodes.

tail.title: Kokoro-FastAPI 0.7.2 - fixes FLAC truncation at finalize, patches a Starlette DoS
tail.summary: Kokoro-FastAPI 0.7.2 fixes FLAC losing its tail at finalize and bumps FastAPI/Starlette past a FileResponse DoS CVE. Patrick's audio-overview and long-form-audio skills run on Kokoro, so the truncated-tail fix is one he would actually have hit on long chapter renders.

tail.title: human-writing - a de-AI-ing writing skill that hit 2k stars in four days
tail.summary: A Chinese-language skill aimed squarely at making AI prose read like a specific person talking rather than a model - nearly 2,000 stars in four days. Patrick runs mimesis for exactly this problem in English; the interesting part is comparing what heuristics another team reached for independently.

tail.title: ADNovelFactory - a staged spec-to-audit pipeline for long-form novel drafting
tail.summary: A macOS long-form novel workflow that runs from an S0 specification through to an L6 audit and TXT export - i.e. it treats a novel as a staged artefact with a review gate rather than one long generation. Structurally close to how Patrick already thinks about The Basilisk, and worth raiding for the stage definitions even if he never runs it.

tail.title: slate - a prompt studio for AI filmmaking that tracks shot continuity
tail.summary: A prompt studio for AI filmmaking: plan shots, direct coverage, and hold continuity across generations. The continuity-tracking problem it solves for shots is the same one that breaks AI-assisted prose across chapters, and the UI is a decent argument for how to surface it.

tail.title: Monty Python and the Holy Grail, in alphabetical order
tail.summary: Every word of Monty Python and the Holy Grail, re-cut into alphabetical order. A pure act of obsessive editing that has nothing to do with AI and is better for it - the sort of thing that reminds you constraint-based art predates the models by decades.

tail.title: Likeface - generate a real installable typeface from a description or a photo
tail.summary: Generate an installable font from a text description, a photo containing five or more letters of a typeface you want, or an uploaded TTF/OTF. Roughly $6 per base font for 500+ glyphs with bold and italic. A concrete, bounded creative-AI product rather than a demo.

tail.title: A free open-source browser pixel art editor with animation and auto-tiling
tail.summary: A free browser pixel-art editor with layers, mirror drawing, infinite canvas, frame-by-frame animation with onion skin, and auto-tiling tilesets - no install, no signup, no watermark, MIT frontend. Genuinely complete rather than a landing page.

tail.title: Music to confuse AI might be the next new genre
tail.summary: CDM on musicians deliberately writing material designed to poison or confuse AI training and detection - adversarial examples as an aesthetic movement rather than a research artefact. A nice case of the adversarial-robustness literature leaking into culture.

tail.title: 808 Day: free Roland e-Bjook, NTS Radio jams, animation
tail.summary: 808 Day - free Roland e-Bjook, NTS Radio jams, and animation, on the annual 8/08 celebration of the TR-808. Pure delight, and a reminder that the drum machine that defined three genres was a commercial failure discontinued after three years.

tail.title: radio-dj - a 24/7 AI radio station in Go with live ducking and LLM banter
tail.summary: 24/7 AI-DJ radio in Go: a persistent ffmpeg-to-Icecast pipeline with live ducking, LLM banter between tracks, and a real broadcast chain. The engineering is the interesting part - this is a radio station, not a chatbot with a music button.

tail.title: Strata-Studio - hand your DAW controls to an AI agent
tail.summary: Lets an AI agent drive your DAW so you can stay on the musical decisions rather than the mouse work. The agent-controls-a-creative-application pattern is one of the more genuinely promising directions for creative AI, and far more interesting than another text-to-audio model.

tail.title: QWERTY MIDI - an isomorphic MIDI controller built on a normal keyboard
tail.summary: An isomorphic-layout MIDI controller driven from a normal QWERTY keyboard, where the interval between two notes is the same physical shape regardless of key. A small, opinionated instrument-design argument in the form of a working tool.

tail.title: demake - write once, compile to any retro game console ROM
tail.summary: One source project that compiles to any retro console ROM, via a declarative language the author invented called Demotic. It started as a tool to solve a real gen-AI problem: models can draw retro-styled sprites but cannot honour exact hardware pixel and palette constraints. The fan-out to arbitrary handheld specs is the payoff.

tail.title: textlog - a text-only, no-JS microblogging platform
tail.summary: A quiet, text-only, open-source microblogging platform with no JavaScript. 187 points and 72 comments largely arguing about whether the constraint is principle or affectation - which is itself the interesting read.

tail.title: Clippy for macOS - the retro paperclip, now with actual computer use
tail.summary: Clippy resurrected as a floating retro paperclip with real computer-use capability behind it. The joke and the capability are the same artefact, which is the best version of this kind of thing.

tail.title: Higher-dimensional lattices unfolded into the 2D plane
tail.summary: Higher-dimensional lattices unfolded into the 2D plane, explorable in the browser - press N for a new experiment, A to learn how it works. Pure mathematical toy, and a good five minutes.

tail.title: Building my own smart roller shades - PCB, firmware, OpenSCAD, and one fatal alignment flaw
tail.summary: A 2019-2020 project finally written up: custom PCB, ESP8266 firmware, Hall-effect position sensor, parameterised OpenSCAD parts, AWS IoT, and Google Home integration - plus an honest admission that a mechanical alignment flaw would eventually have torn the drive wheel off. Good writeups include the failure.

tail.title: CrossPlay - games and puzzles designed for e-readers and their slow refresh
tail.summary: Games, puzzles, and tools built for e-ink readers - designed around slow refresh rather than fighting it. A nice example of designing to a constraint instead of treating it as a defect.

tail.title: Give your jailbroken Kindle a real domain name on your network
tail.summary: Give your jailbroken Kindle a real hostname on your local network via mDNS. Tiny, and exactly the kind of thing that makes an old device usable again.

tail.title: starboard - a terminal permanently glued beside the macOS dock
tail.summary: A terminal permanently docked beside the macOS Dock - explicitly not a Quake-style hotkey overlay, but a persistent always-there strip. An argument about where a terminal should live, shipped as software.

tail.title: How will the 12 August eclipse look from your exact address?
tail.summary: Type your address and see exactly how the 12 August total solar eclipse will look from there - total over Iceland and northern Spain, over 90% across much of France. France-only for now. Genuinely useful for anyone in the path.

tail.title: MusicMonitor - your spare monitor as a Spotify now-playing display
tail.summary: Turns a spare monitor into a full-screen Spotify now-playing display that hides itself the moment your mouse enters that screen. Built with Codex, and a good example of the small-personal-tool category agents are genuinely good for.

tail.title: Two years designing a mechanical Magic Keyboard
tail.summary: Two years designing a mechanical version of Apple's Magic Keyboard - the top Show HN of the window at 295 points and 241 comments. The writeup on tolerances and why the obvious approach fails is the substance here.

tail.title: My AI agent built and shipped a browser game on its own
tail.summary: An author's agent built and shipped a playable browser game end to end, itch.io page included. Low points, but exactly the sort of claim worth checking yourself - the artefact is right there and playable.

tail.title: tidewright - a GPU-only 3D sandcastle simulator, no engine, no libraries
tail.summary: A 3D sandcastle simulator running entirely on the GPU with no engine and no libraries. Deeply pointless, technically impressive, and the kind of thing that is more fun than another agent framework.

tail.title: emeraldian - a terminal UI for your Obsidian vault, backlinks and all
tail.summary: A terminal UI for an Obsidian vault: live-preview notes, backlinks, images, all without leaving the shell. If Patrick keeps notes in Obsidian-compatible markdown, this puts them one keystroke from where he already works.

tail.title: pyroclear - clear your terminal with a wall of ASCII fire
tail.summary: Clears your terminal with a crackling wall of ASCII flames. That is the entire product.

tail.title: autoclip - a local-first AI video clipper, long video in, captioned clips out
tail.summary: Local-first open-source AI video clipper: long video in, caption-burned speaker-tracked clips out. Runs locally, which matters if the source material is anything you would not upload.

tail.title: hyperframes - agents write HTML, you get rendered video
tail.summary: Write HTML, render video - a rendering pipeline built for agents to produce video by emitting markup rather than driving a timeline. The agent-friendly interface choice is the interesting bit: HTML is a format models are extremely good at.

tail.title: LichtFeld-Studio - a full editing environment for 3D Gaussian Splatting
tail.summary: Train, inspect, edit, automate, and export 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from one application. Gaussian splatting has mostly lived in research scripts; a real editing environment around it is what makes it usable.

tail.title: Invidious - the alternative YouTube front-end spikes 1,200 stars in a week
tail.summary: Invidious, the alternative YouTube front end, spiked ~1,225 stars this week. Directly relevant to Patrick's planned WatchFeed/Signal Watch project, which needs a way to pull YouTube metadata without the official surface.

tail.title: A physicist rigged his pet hamster's wheel to upload to Strava
tail.summary: A physicist rigged his pet hamster's wheel to upload to Strava. 382 points. This is the correct use of engineering.

tail.title: The title cards in Blade Runner are amazing
tail.summary: Rands on why the title cards in Blade Runner are so good - typography, pacing, and the confidence to hold a frame. Relevant to anyone thinking about how a piece of work announces itself.

tail.title: NASA figured out how to keep Voyager 2 running for another year
